\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Iterative Reduction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.IterativeReduction
\section{Overview}

This module carries out Steps 8--9 of the LMN argument: it applies the one-step
switching/compression mechanism repeatedly across all intermediate circuit layers
(reducing depth $d$ down to depth $2$), and combines the per-stage failure
probabilities into a single union bound of order $s\cdot(1/2)^l$. The arithmetic
package shows that with $l=\log_2(2s/\varepsilon)$ the total failure probability is
at most $\varepsilon/2$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

  {LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}
  {pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{1}
Fix positive integers $n$ and $l$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_{s_i}$ be DNF formulas on $n$
variables, each of width at most $l$, and each in reduced form: no term repeats a
literal, and within a term any two literals on the same variable coincide, so every
variable occurs at most once in each term. Let $p$ be a real parameter with $0 < p \le
1$ and $p \le \tfrac{1}{40\,l}$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ of the
$n$ variables, which independently leaves each variable free with probability $p$ and
otherwise fixes it to $0$ or $1$ each with probability $(1-p)/2$. Then the probability
that some restricted gate fails to be computed by a narrow CNF — that is, for some $i$
there is no CNF formula $\psi$ of width at most $l$ satisfying $\psi(x) =
g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ for every assignment $x$ — is at most
\[
  s_i\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n p}{3}\right)\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision-tree depth of restricted DNF gates]
\lean{LMN.subsequent_step_dtDepth}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008}
\label{LMN.subsequent_step_dtDepth}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.one_step_dtDepth_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$ and a positive integer $l$, and let $\phi_1, \dots, \phi_s$ be
DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, each of width at most $l$ and each written so
that no variable occurs more than once in any single term — that is, no term repeats a
literal, and no term contains two literals on the same variable. Let $p \in \bbr$
satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40 l}$ (so in particular $p \le 1$). Then a Bernoulli$(p)$
random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables satisfies, with probability at least
\[
  1 - s\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right)\right),
\]
that for every $i$ the restricted function $x \mapsto \phi_i$ evaluated on the
coordinates left free by $\rho$ (with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$) has
decision-tree depth at most $l$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Summing per-layer failure bounds]
\lean{LMN.multi_stage_failure_bound}
\label{LMN.multi_stage_failure_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha \ge 0$, let $s \in \bbn$, and consider $m$ stages with layer sizes $\ell_0,
\ldots, \ell_{m-1} \in \bbn$ whose total does not exceed $s$, i.e. $\sum_{i} \ell_i \le
s$. Suppose real numbers $b_0, \ldots, b_{m-1}$ satisfy $b_i \le \ell_i\,\alpha$ for
every $i$. Then $\sum_{i} b_i \le s\,\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Union bound for restriction probabilities]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_union_bound_fin}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_union_bound_fin}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg'}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a parameter $p \in \bbr$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $A_0, \dots, A_{m-1}$ be
finitely many events on restrictions of $n$ variables. Under a Bernoulli($p$) random
restriction, the probability that at least one of the events $A_i$ occurs is at most the
sum of the probabilities of the individual events:
\[
\bbP_p\!\left[\exists i,\ A_i(\rho)\right] \le \sum_{i=0}^{m-1}
\bbP_p\!\left[A_i(\rho)\right],
\]
where $\bbP_p[\cdot]$ denotes the Bernoulli event probability at parameter $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Iterative dominant-term bound (conclusion unspecified)]
\lean{LMN.iterative_dominant_term_bound}
\label{LMN.iterative_dominant_term_bound}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b003
}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a natural number $m$ and layer sizes $\ell_0,\dots,\ell_{m-1}\in\bbn$, and let
$s\in\bbn$ with $s>0$ bound their total, $\sum_{i} \ell_i \le s$. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be
a real number. Under these hypotheses the intended conclusion is that, on setting
$l=\log_2(2s/\varepsilon)$, the total weighted contribution is controlled by
$\varepsilon/2$, namely $\sum_{i} \ell_i\,(1/2)^{l}\le \varepsilon/2$; however, the
formal statement leaves both the value $l$ and the conclusion as placeholders, so it
asserts no mathematical claim beyond these hypotheses.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A union bound for two-stage Bernoulli restrictions]
\lean{LMN.two_stage_composed_union_bound}
\label{LMN.two_stage_composed_union_bound}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight}
Fix $n$, and let $p,q$ be real parameters with $0\le p\le 1$ and $0\le q\le 1$. For a
parameter $r$ write $w_r(\rho)$ for the Bernoulli weight of a restriction $\rho$ on $n$
variables at parameter $r$, and write $\bbP_r[E]$ for the Bernoulli event probability of
a predicate $E$ on restrictions at parameter $r$. Then for any two predicates $A$ and
$B$ on restrictions of $n$ variables,
\[
\sum_{\rho_1} w_p(\rho_1)\,\bbP_q\!\big[\,\rho_2 \mapsto A(\rho_1)\lor B(\rho_2)\,\big]
\;\le\; \bbP_p[A] + \bbP_q[B],
\]
where the inner sum ranges over all restrictions $\rho_1$ on $n$ variables and, for each
fixed $\rho_1$, the predicate $\rho_2 \mapsto A(\rho_1)\lor B(\rho_2)$ holds at a
second-stage restriction $\rho_2$ exactly when $A$ holds at $\rho_1$ or $B$ holds at
$\rho_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Abstract iterative reduction bound]
\lean{LMN.abstract_iterative_reduction}
\label{LMN.abstract_iterative_reduction}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{LMN.iterative_dominant_term_bound}
\difficulty{2}
Let $m$ be a natural number and let $\ell_0,\dots,\ell_{m-1}$ be natural numbers (the
layer sizes) whose sum is at most a positive integer $s$. Fix a real number
$\varepsilon>0$, and suppose that $b_0,\dots,b_{m-1}$ are real numbers satisfying
\[
b_i \;\le\; \ell_i\cdot\left(\tfrac12\right)^{\log_2\!\left(2s/\varepsilon\right)}
\qquad\text{for every } i.
\]
Then $\sum_{i} b_i \le \varepsilon/2$.
\end{theorem}
